chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

“The muhsan is flogged one hundred lashes and stoned; and whoever has not become muhsan is flogged one hundred lashes and is not exiled; and the woman who has been married off but has not been consummated with, is flogged one hundred lashes and exiled.”

key_terms.أُمْلِكَتْ: has been given in marriage through conclusion of the marriage contract
key_terms.اَلْمُحْصَنُ: a legally protected married person in the context of zina rulings
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: is flogged as a prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.يُدْخَلْ بِهَا: the marriage has been consummated with her
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: is stoned as part of the hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for zina for the muhsan and the non-muhsan in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning the hadd of zina, distinguishing between the muhsan and one who is not muhsan, and also mentioning the case of a woman whose marriage contract has been concluded but the marriage has not yet been consummated. Its significance lies in its classification of legal consequences according to marital status and consummation.
